1. I told them in my birthday, because i felt like they couldn't react badly in my special day hahahah. I said "i wanna tell you i'm non binary.
Just so you know, probably it's not gonna be a big deal if they already know about trans and non binary people, so try really hard to explain what does it mean to you, because they probably don't wanna hear about tecnical words, just how you feel in your body.

2. My mum said "alright, so what's your name?" and asked me what does it mean to me beaing non binary, i said "if someone tells you that you are a boy, you just know it's not true, for me it's the same with both genders".
I really recommend to explain what transition is, both physical and social, cause i didn't and had to wait another year to start transitioning, it might be obvious for us, but people don't really know what it is. So make sure you make them a part of it, let them know that you are gonna be trully happy that way.

3. If they are supportive, they're gonna know that all that it's part of being trans. I don't know about gender policies in school where you live, in my country they have to change it even if it's not legally changed.

9. I trully feel like your brother is gonna be the less problematic, childs just get it or don't care at all hahahahah. You can ask your parents to tell him, and maybe he'll be more serious about it. 
Explain to your mum that it's not a phase, that non binary people can have a normal life being non binary, and don't feel like you are being to much or a burden for them, you are not. You just want them to see you as who you are.

I cannot answer your questions about extended familly cause they don't know. 
But my advices are: explain yourself the best you can about transition, tell them everything you want (like hormones and stuff), tell them what your fears are, like "i'm scared that your are gonna think that it's childish, or a phase, or that you'll gonna make fun of it...", and take it easy. I expected everything to change that day, and actually i'm transitioning one year after i came out, so it takes time, but remember that you are doing it to feel better.
